title: My first finalized Vibecoding project
author: RadiantExternal8752
selftext:
This is the first game I’ve developed using Vibecoding. I’m very close to releasing the demo, and the core loop is working well right now; I’m just working on the visual polish.

During the auto-battler segments, the opposing character offers three card choices after every few kills; they extend or shorten the game entirely at their own whim, mock us if we make a mistake, change the rules, sometimes help us and sometimes make things harder, play card tricks on us, set card traps, and do a whole host of other things I can't even recall right now. As you can see in the video: We don't pick the card they suggest, and we fall into a trap because of it; then we pick the next card they offer, and we fall into a trap \*because\* we picked it. I really tried to create a game that highlights mind games and surprises. What do you think?

replies.author: RadiantExternal8752
replies.body: Aside from a few placeholder visuals in the video, here is how I handled the rest: For the backgrounds, I listed every detail in separate notes and used them to craft very long, detailed prompts; I also locked in a specific visual style for the objects placed over the backgrounds and maintained that style throughout the generation process. I defined every aspect of the main character's appearance—from their hat and shirt down to the playing card tucked into the rolled-up left sleeve—and generated the character model using AI. To ensure smooth animation based on this main look, I generated frame-by-frame transitions (at least 6–8 frames per animation) and created a spritesheet. For the version of our hero that appears on the game board, I created a 4x3 frame grid—covering idle, walk, hit, and death states—step-by-step and added it to the game as a spritesheet. If you have any questions about the details, I’d be happy to explain further.

replies.author: RadiantExternal8752
replies.body: It was incredibly helpful for me to have the AI—which I used right from the start—map out a roadmap for the entire project and list every step involved. Claude excels at this. I would then identify potential issues at each stage and resolve them before moving on to the next step. Regarding image generation, clearly defining the visual style, extracting all the details of that style, and using that specific style prompt for every generated image eliminates inconsistencies in UI and stylization.

replies.author: DarknessYoshi
replies.body: So, since I have it running night now. Best will be to divide it in segments, for example, rolling a dice and move character . Then for other segment, nos battle phase only. And in the end, integrate everything? Or should I tell cloud that we will do it in phases or will it automatically detect it?

replies.author: RadiantExternal8752
replies.body: Yes, we definitely need to tell Claude that this is a project that will proceed step-by-step, and that we must move to the next step only after confirming that the current one has been completed successfully. We also need to obtain the full sequence of steps in a "roadmap" file so that we can refer back to it in a new chat session once the current one becomes too long.
